CHIEF COMPLAINT
Acne on the face

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Kayla Ward is a 18-year-old female presenting with acne located on the face that started approximately two years ago and is present most every day. She reports no associated symptoms including itching, bleeding, or pain. Current management includes use of Persa-Gel and regular face washing, which she reports is somewhat helpful. Patient notes that acne is not significant on chest or back. Mother reports the biggest flare occurred when patient started school sports in the fall due to sweating. Patient denies acne flares with menstrual cycle and reports having regular periods for approximately two years. Mother notes patient has been diligent with facial care regimen but desired better results.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies itching, bleeding, or pain associated with acne. Denies acne flares with menses. Reports regular menstrual periods. No other systemic symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
None reported

MEDICATIONS
Persa-Gel (over-the-counter benzoyl peroxide)
ELF Super Clarity Cleanser
Facial toner

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives with parents and sister. Pets include one dog, one bird, and bunnies. Currently in 7th grade. Participates in basketball, volleyball, and tap dance. Uses sunscreen SPF 30 in summer.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Full exam performed except areas under underwear and bra. Multiple benign nevi on trunk and extremities. Scattered skin-colored papules. Open and closed comedones present. Erythematous papules on face, primarily on forehead with some on central cheeks and chin. Chest and back relatively spared. Remainder of examination normal.

RESULTS
Mild to moderate acne, mostly comedonal with small inflammatory component. Multiple benign moles on arms, legs, back, and abdomen with no worrisome features.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Mild to moderate facial acne, comedonal with inflammatory component. Plan: (1) Morning skincare: Wash face with mild cleanser, apply noncomedogenic moisturizer with SPF 30 or higher. (2) Evening skincare: Wash face with mild cleanser, allow to dry, apply adapalene 0.1% cream in thin layer to areas of acne, starting a few nights per week and gradually increasing to nightly use. Follow with Persa-Gel in thin layer and noncomedogenic moisturizer. (3) Educate patient on potential side effects of adapalene including sensitivity, dryness, and irritation; emphasize need for sunscreen use when outdoors. (4) Alternative: If adapalene not covered or too expensive, patient may use over-the-counter retinoid gel. (5) Follow-up visit in 6 months to assess progress. Patient instructed to call office with any questions or concerns before next visit.
